description: Compute whether a set of web features clears an explicit browserslist target query. Compares up to 20 features per call; up to 100 may be sent, and entries past the 20th come back unevaluated in omitted_features for the next call. Every call evaluates the whole query: each feature gets a verdict, the count of failing targets, those targets grouped into runs of consecutive query targets per browser in failing_ranges, and its own evaluated and unevaluated target counts with the share of tracked traffic each covers. The target rows behind those numbers — which release each target maps to, which targets were not evaluated and why, and the failing and unevaluated targets of each feature, a failing row carrying the prefix, alternative name, or flag behind its verdict — cover at most ten query targets per call; page through them with target_offset and target_limit, and the verdicts, coverage, and totals stay identical on every page. A target counts as evaluated only where compatibility data was read for it, so a feature clears only when every target in the query was evaluated and supports it, and is inconclusive otherwise — a query that includes a browser with no compatibility data, as "defaults" does, never clears. A BCD key is judged on its own per-browser support. A web-features id spanning several keys, such as grid, is judged on the release web-features lists for the feature as a whole in each Baseline core browser, as support_source says; its other browsers are not evaluated.

features.description: Entries to compare, each a browser-compat-data key such as css.selectors.has or a web-features id such as has, 1 to 200 characters. The first 20 are compared per call; up to 100 are accepted, and entries past the 20th are returned unevaluated in omitted_features. More than 100 entries, or an empty or longer entry anywhere in the list, is rejected against this schema; a whitespace-only entry anywhere returns invalid_feature_input. Call browsercompat_search_features first for any entry whose key you do not already know.

resolve.description: When true, an entry that is neither a key nor an id falls back to the search index, such as "Container queries (size)" or "Element.prototype.animate". Its best exact matches are accepted only when they name one feature: a single key resolves to that key and is judged on it, several keys of one web-features feature resolve to the feature and are judged on its feature-level support with compat_keys, and matches spanning two features are a miss. Off by default so a typo returns a miss you can correct rather than a confident answer about the wrong feature.

target_limit.description: How many query targets this page covers, at most 10 per call; a value from 11 to 1000 is served as 10, and the cap enrichment field reports the size applied. It bounds every list of target rows in the response and never the evaluation: verdicts, coverage, and totals always describe the whole query.

target_offset.description: Zero-based position in the target list of the query at which this page of target rows starts. Pass the nextOffset of the previous response to continue. An offset at or past the number of targets returns the whole-query verdicts and totals with no target rows.

targets.description: A browserslist query, for example "defaults" or "> 0.5%, last 2 versions", 1 to 500 characters. Required: with no query browserslist would read config from the process working directory rather than from your project.

name: browsercompat_compare_support

all_clear.description: True only when every feature clears, which requires every target in the query to have been evaluated for it — for a feature judged on web-features’ feature-level support, every target must be a Baseline core browser. Any entry in omitted_features forces false.

attribution.description: Required attribution for the caniuse-derived coverage figures in this response.

cap.description: The page size applied: target_limit, or 10 when target_limit was above 10.

comparable_features.description: How many entries in features were compared against the targets, on a key or on web-features’ feature-level support. A miss or an ambiguous entry is not comparable; at 0 nothing was evaluated.

data_version.description: Vintage of each bundled dataset behind this answer.

bcd_generated.description: ISO 8601 timestamp the browser-compat-data snapshot was generated at.

browserslist.description: Version of the bundled browserslist query resolver.

caniuse_lite.description: Version of the bundled caniuse-lite snapshot.

web_features.description: Version of the bundled web-features snapshot.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `invalid_target_query`: browserslist rejected the targets query. `no_targets_resolved`: The query matched no browser versions at all, or only agents with no browser-compat-data counterpart. A mapped agent whose version token does not resolve is reported in unchecked_targets instead. `invalid_feature_input`: An entry in features is whitespace-only, including an entry past the 20th. An empty or over-200-character entry is rejected against the input schema instead. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

evaluated_targets_total.description: Query targets evaluated for every compared feature, across every page. evaluated_targets_total plus unchecked_targets_total is the number of targets in the query.

nextOffset.description: The target_offset of the next page. Present only while targets remain past this page.

offsetNotice.description: Why this page carries no target rows, and the offsets that do.

omitted_features.description: Entries past the first 20, verbatim and in input order, that were not compared. Present only when the call sent more than 20; pass them as features in the next call.

query_echo.description: The targets query as the server parsed it.

results.description: Per-feature verdicts and totals over the whole query for the first 20 entries, each with its own target rows for this page.

items.description: One result per evaluated entry, in input order.

compat_keys.description: The browser-compat-data keys a web-features id owns, its first 10 in declaration order: present when the id spans more than one key and was judged on its feature-level support, and as an empty list on an ambiguous verdict. compat_keys_total counts all of them; call browsercompat_get_feature with the id for the rest. Call again with one of them for a key-level verdict that also covers non-core browsers.

compat_keys_total.description: Every browser-compat-data key the id owns. Present with compat_keys.

evaluated_coverage_percent.description: Share of tracked global traffic the targets evaluated for this feature cover.

evaluated_total.description: Query targets this feature has compatibility data for, across the whole query.

failing_ranges.description: Every failing target across the whole query, grouped into runs: consecutive query targets of one browserslist agent that fail with the same verdict, in query order — agents in browserslist’s order, newest run first. A run breaks at any target that passed or was not evaluated for this feature, so it spans only versions the query contains. The counts sum to failing_total, and the list is the same on every page. Empty when nothing failed.

items.description: A run of consecutive failing query targets.

agent.description: browserslist agent id of every target in the run.

newest.description: Version token of the run’s first, newest target.

oldest.description: Version token of the run’s last, oldest target; equals newest for a run of one.

verdict.description: Why this target failed. From a key: partial means the implementation does not meet the mandatory specified behavior, prefixed means it only ships under a vendor prefix or a different name, flagged means it only works behind a preference or runtime flag, removed means it shipped and was later removed before this target version, unsupported means it was never added, preview_only means it only works in a preview channel. From web-features’ feature-level support: before_feature_support means the target predates the release web-features lists for the feature, no_feature_support means web-features lists no release of this core browser for the feature — which also covers a feature it lists no release for at all, such as a discontinued one (mutation-events) that older releases shipped; call again with one of compat_keys for a key-level verdict on such a target.

failing_targets.description: The failing targets among the query targets on this page, with the verdict that caused each. A row judged on a key also carries the fields of the support statement behind its verdict — version_added, prefix, alternative_name, flags, and the rest — each only when that statement has it; an unsupported or preview_only row, and a row judged on web-features’ feature-level support, carry none. Empty on a page that holds none even when failing_total is above zero.

items.description: A target this feature does not clear.

agent.description: browserslist agent id the target came from.

alternative_name.description: Entirely different name the feature is implemented under.

bcd_browser.description: browser-compat-data browser the agent maps to.

bcd_version.description: browser-compat-data release the token mapped to, or null when it predates them all.

flags.description: Flags gating support in this browser.

items.description: A flag that must be configured for support.

name.description: Name of the flag or preference to configure.

type.description: Whether the gate is a user preference or a runtime flag.

value_to_set.description: Value the flag must be set to.

partial.description: True when the implementation does not meet the mandatory specified behavior.

prefix.description: Vendor prefix the feature ships under.

verdict.description: Why this target failed. From a key: partial means the implementation does not meet the mandatory specified behavior, prefixed means it only ships under a vendor prefix or a different name, flagged means it only works behind a preference or runtime flag, removed means it shipped and was later removed before this target version, unsupported means it was never added, preview_only means it only works in a preview channel. From web-features’ feature-level support: before_feature_support means the target predates the release web-features lists for the feature, no_feature_support means web-features lists no release of this core browser for the feature — which also covers a feature it lists no release for at all, such as a discontinued one (mutation-events) that older releases shipped; call again with one of compat_keys for a key-level verdict on such a target.

version_added_is_upper_bound.description: True when the data says support arrived at or before version_added, not exactly at it.

version_last.description: Last release that still supported the feature.

version_token.description: Version token browserslist produced for that agent.

failing_total.description: Failing targets across the whole query. Present when the feature was compared, as are the six fields after it.

found.description: True when the feature string resolved to a tracked entry.

guidance.description: What to do next on a miss or an ambiguous verdict.

input.description: The feature string as the caller sent it.

name.description: web-features display name for the feature.

baseline_id.description: The web-features id this resolved to, or null when no web-features entry covers the key.

bcd_key.description: The single browser-compat-data key this resolved to, or null when the web-features id spans more than one key or owns none.

input.description: The feature string as the caller sent it, trimmed.

resolved_via.description: Which step of the resolution order matched: bcd_key or web_features_id for an exact match, web_features_id_normalized when it matched only after lowercasing, redirect when the input pointed to a browser-compat-data entry that has moved or split, or search when resolve was true and the best exact matches in the search index all named one feature or key — treat a search match as a best guess, not a confirmed key.

resolved_as.description: How the feature string was matched, or null on a miss.

support_source.description: What the verdict was judged on. bcd_key: one browser-compat-data key’s per-browser support. web_features_feature: for an id spanning more than one key, web-features’ own release per Baseline core browser for the feature as a whole — never a combination of its keys, and a key can differ from it either way; browsers outside the core set are then not evaluated. Present on every compared result.

unchecked_coverage_percent.description: Share of tracked global traffic the targets not evaluated for this feature cover.

unchecked_targets.description: The targets not evaluated for this feature among the query targets on this page, each with its reason.

items.description: A target this feature was not evaluated against.

reason.description: no_bcd_browser when the agent has no browser-compat-data counterpart, unknown_version when the token maps to no release, no_bcd_data when a compared key records nothing for that browser, no_feature_level_data when a feature judged on web-features’ feature-level support has no answer for the target — a browser outside the Baseline core set, or a release before a ≤ bound — so call again with one of its compat_keys for a key-level answer, no_comparable_feature when every entry in features was a miss or ambiguous so nothing was compared. In the top-level list a target unchecked by several compared features takes the reason of the first of them.

usage_percent.description: Share of tracked global traffic this target covers.

version_token.description: Version token browserslist produced for that agent.

unchecked_total.description: Query targets not evaluated for this feature, across the whole query. evaluated_total plus unchecked_total is the number of targets in the query.

verdict.description: Judged over the whole query, never over one page. fails when any evaluated target does not support the feature; inconclusive when nothing failed but at least one target in the query was not evaluated for this feature, including when none was; clears only when every target in the query was evaluated and supports it; miss when the entry did not resolve; ambiguous when the web-features id owns no browser-compat-data keys, so there is no support data to judge.

shown.description: Number of query targets this page covers.

target_coverage_percent.description: Share of tracked global traffic covered by the targets evaluated for every compared feature; 0 when no feature was comparable.

targets_resolved.description: The mapping inventory for the query targets on this page: each target that maps onto a browser-compat-data release, and whether it was evaluated. A target with no mapping appears only in unchecked_targets.

items.description: A target that mapped onto a concrete release.

bcd_browser.description: browser-compat-data browser the agent maps to.

bcd_release_index.description: Release ordinal used for comparison; -1 when the token predates every release.

bcd_version.description: browser-compat-data release the token mapped to, or null when it predates them all.

evaluated.description: True when every compared feature has compatibility data for this target. False when at least one compared feature records nothing for its browser or has no feature-level data for it, or when no feature in the call was comparable — the target then also appears in unchecked_targets. Mapping onto a release is not evaluation.

version_token.description: Version token browserslist produced for that agent.

targets_resolved_total.description: Query targets that map onto a browser-compat-data release, across every page.

totalCount.description: Number of targets the query resolved to, across every page.

truncated.description: True when more query targets remain past this page.

uncheckedNotice.description: How many of the query targets were not evaluated for every compared feature, the agents they belong to, and their combined usage share.

unchecked_coverage_percent.description: Share of tracked global traffic covered by the targets counted in unchecked_targets_total.

unchecked_targets.description: The query targets on this page that were not evaluated for every compared feature, each with the reason.

items.description: A target that was not evaluated.

reason.description: no_bcd_browser when the agent has no browser-compat-data counterpart, unknown_version when the token maps to no release, no_bcd_data when a compared key records nothing for that browser, no_feature_level_data when a feature judged on web-features’ feature-level support has no answer for the target — a browser outside the Baseline core set, or a release before a ≤ bound — so call again with one of its compat_keys for a key-level answer, no_comparable_feature when every entry in features was a miss or ambiguous so nothing was compared. In the top-level list a target unchecked by several compared features takes the reason of the first of them.

usage_percent.description: Share of tracked global traffic this target covers.

version_token.description: Version token browserslist produced for that agent.

unchecked_targets_total.description: Query targets not evaluated for every compared feature, across every page.
